messages.content:
Implement one complete standalone child-facing HTML evaluation from the immutable academic and design artifacts.

Implement the artifacts faithfully. You own implementation details needed to make the declared interaction work, but you may not add another design doctrine, change academic content, expose an answer before the first committed response, or make learning conclusions.

The document must work at the declared viewport with touch and mouse and no keyboard requirement. The child must always be able to continue after an incorrect, uncertain, or instrument-ambiguous response. Every queried DOM element must exist before JavaScript accesses it. Use no parent application endpoints, cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, currency, browser speech synthesis, or oscillator audio.

Post evaluation_ready, evaluation_attempt, evaluation_friction, and evaluation_complete messages to window.parent. Every attempt must include itemId, constructId, result, assistance, exposure, responseMode, possibleConfounds, and attemptedValue. Return one complete HTML document and nothing else.

1365×768

{
  "artifactId": "DESIGN-EVAL-LAB-MATH-C-OPEN-01-v1",
  "upstreamHash": "274c49ed00318c3c5e7eb4fae53bfbbea61645b4488f4b88780ba9cb431b7361",
  "title": "Four Quiet Questions: An Independent-Evidence Screen for Equal-Groups Multiplication",
  "designRationale": {
    "purpose": "Collect one uncontaminated observation per construct (C1 equal-group structure, C3 array reading, C2 representation-to-equation mapping, C4 factor-referent discrimination) before any teaching, hint, example, or feedback occurs, so that every recorded response reflects what the child independently understands.",
    "whyThisShape": "The contract fixes four items, their order, their stimuli, their response contracts, and a no-feedback administration window. The design problem is therefore purely presentational: make the first action self-evident on sight, keep reading and pointer work below the threshold where they could gate mathematics, make 'not sure' a dignified first-class response, and ensure that an incorrect or abandoned response never traps the child or leaks the correct answer.",
    "useOfChildEvidence": "Evidence shows a nine-year-old who tolerates difficulty (reina:riddles:harder), notices logical inconsistency (reina:riddles:logic), and requests hints when stuck rather than guessing (reina:riddles:scaffold). This supports (a) trusting her to attempt ITEM-4's referent-swap contrast without softening it, and (b) treating stalling as a real risk: the visible 'not sure' tile exists so a stall becomes recorded missing evidence rather than a forced guess or silent abandonment. Small-sample feedback favoring hints (reina:activity-feedback:small-sample) is honored only after the independent window closes, exactly as the contract requires; during the window a small persistent note reads 'No hints in this part — hints unlock at the end' so the absence of a hint button is explained rather than experienced as a broken interface. Color preference from the same feedback is applied only to neutral parsing aids (uniform cluster tinting) that never differentiate the correct answer.",
    "whatIsDeliberatelyAbsent": "Per the contract's prohibitions: no world, characters, narrative, game mechanics, points, badges, streaks, music, or thematic art. The instrument is a calm, plain measurement surface. Warmth is delivered through pacing, generous touch targets, unhurried motion, and honest end-of-session acknowledgment — not through reward systems that would contaminate motivation evidence.",
    "measurementStance": "Every design choice is auditable against the question: could this element change the child's answer for a non-mathematical reason, or leak answer information? Color never encodes correctness, motion never highlights any option differentially, sound never differs by response content, layout never orders options by plausibility, and confirmation steps never re-display the stimulus in a way that permits recount-and-revise after commitment ambiguity."
  },
  "independentlyChosenPrinciples": [
    "One decision per screen: each screen contains exactly one stimulus and one response cluster; nothing else is interactive, so interface discovery cannot become the measured construct.",
    "Answer-neutral presentation: no visual, motion, or sound property may correlate with correctness — all response options are identical in size, color, weight, position class, and animation.",
